findings.certainty: high that the test is tautological with respect to the helper; the production call site can regress without any test failing.
findings.evidence: The test invokes the helper directly (`AIChatViewModel.prependFallbackInfoBlock(info, to: message, committedBlockCount: &committedBlockCount, previousCommittedBlockCount: &previousCommittedBlockCount)`) and then asserts committedBlockCount == 2 && previousCommittedBlockCount == 2 — i.e. it re-asserts the helper body's own `+= 1` on both inout parameters. It never sets viewModel.prevCommittedBlockCount and never reaches applyFallbackSwitch, so the production wiring (`Self.prependFallbackInfoBlock(...); self.committedBlockCount = committedBlockCount`) is not covered by any test.

findings.certainty: high that the Stop-after-Retry timing path and the retry->runAgentLoop boundary are unverified by the added tests; no evidence that the implementation is wrong (clearUncommittedStreamTail's clamp and the explicit cursor syncs looked self-consistent on inspection).
findings.evidence: All four retry tests set `viewModel.kernelStatus = .failed("Stop before starting a provider request")` before calling retry(), so retry()'s Task aborts before runAgentLoop (the guard is `if case .failed(let msg) = self.kernelStatus { ... isProcessing = false; return }`, snapshot 2627-2633) and only the pre-stream trim runs; the replacement content is produced by calling processStreamEvents directly. Thus the new `committedBlocks: existingBlockCount` boundary used by retry()'s runAgentLoop and the Stop path that motivated the retry()/resume()/launchRerunAgentLoop cursor sync are not exercised. No test in MinisTests references cancel, handleUserCancelledCleanup, resume() or the SUSPECT/resume branch.

findings.certainty: high that the assignment asymmetry exists; medium that it can produce a user-visible mis-trim, because every stream entry point looked at re-syncs both cursors first — reported as a residual invariant gap rather than a reproduced regression.
findings.evidence: The load path writes only `self.committedBlockCount = lastAssistant.blocks.count`; prevCommittedBlockCount keeps whatever value the VM instance last held (possibly from another message or session), so the two cursors do not describe the same message during that window. The patch added paired syncs at retry(), resume(), launchRerunAgentLoop and injectQueuedPromptsAsNewTurn but not at this load site.

findings.certainty: high for the code asymmetry; low that a current caller can trigger it (defensive/warning path only). Not a proven regression; listed because the task claims every reuse/creation entry point obeys the boundary rule.
findings.evidence: Only the valid-resume branch sets committedBlockCount/prevCommittedBlockCount (= boundary) and effectiveResumeBlocks = boundary; the SUSPECT branch keeps `effectiveResumeBlocks = resumeBlocks` and leaves both instance cursors untouched, yet still falls through to `try await self.runAgentLoop(resumingAt: effectiveResumeAt, committedBlocks: effectiveResumeBlocks)`. That is the one 'reuse an existing assistant message' entry point the patch did not bring under the single boundary rule; prevCommittedBlockCount may also describe a different message if the call is reached mid-session.
